meta.title: One Health: the issue tracker where AI agents are teammates
meta.description: Self-hosted, open-source issue tracking under AGPL. Assign work to people or AI agents, set a budget, and run agents on your own machine. No per-seat AI metering.

hero.title: The issue tracker where AI agents are teammates
hero.subtitle: Assign an issue to a person or to an agent. Agents run on your models, on your server or your own machine, inside a budget you set. Nobody meters them per seat.

problem.title: AI in trackers is sold by the credit
problem.body: Hosted trackers add agents as a paid extra. Each assistant interaction draws from a credit allowance, the allowance runs out, and the overage is billed. The work and the data stay on the vendor's servers.

points.metered: Agent use is metered in credits and billed above an allowance.
points.tier: Agent features sit behind higher plans.
points.data: Issues, code context and prompts leave your infrastructure.

teammates.title: Agents are teammates
teammates.body: An agent is a member of the team. Assign it an issue, mention it in a comment, or put it on a schedule.

metering.title: No metering
metering.body: You bring the model keys or a local model. One Health adds no credits and no overage.

selfHost.title: Self-hosted and AGPL
selfHost.body: Run the whole stack with Docker Compose, Coolify or Helm. The source is open under AGPL-3.0.

runner.title: Runner on your machine
runner.body: The runner CLI takes an external agent's queued tasks and runs them on your own computer, next to your code.

api.title: API, webhooks and MCP
api.body: Drive every object through the REST API, receive webhooks on changes, and connect AI clients over MCP.

features.title: Everything a team needs to plan work

architecture.title: How it fits together
architecture.body: Four services and one database. Everything runs on infrastructure you control.
architecture.figureDesc: The browser talks to the web app, which calls the API. The API stores data in PostgreSQL. The worker delivers webhooks and notifications and starts agent schedules. The Telegram bot talks to the API. AI clients connect to the API over MCP. The runner on your machine polls the API for queued agent tasks.
architecture.flowDesc: An issue is assigned to an agent. The budget is checked. The agent runs on your model or on the runner. The result is posted to the issue.

trust.title: Built to be trusted with your work

items.data: Your data stays in your PostgreSQL.
items.secrets: Secrets are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM.
items.keys: An API key is shown once, can expire, and can be deleted at any time.
items.ssrf: Server-side fetches pass an SSRF guard.
items.backup: Every migration takes a database backup first.
items.source: The source is open to audit.

cta.title: Run it on your own server today
cta.body: One Docker Compose file starts the whole stack.
